claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to know about the child (or children) you're claiming for.

**Could you please tell me:**
1. How old is your child (or children)?
2. What are their names? (This helps me keep track if you have multiple children)

The age is important because:
- Children **under 16** typically qualify automatically
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

What's your child's age?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I've got one child - Alex, who's 18 years old. I just want to check if I'm still eligible to claim for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! So you have Alex who is 18 years old. Since Alex is between 16 and 19, we need to check if they're in approved education or training, as this determines eligibility for this age group.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training situation. 

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or other approved courses)?
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex isn't in education anymore - they finished school and aren't doing any courses or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex isn't currently in education or training, I need to know when they left.

**When did Alex finish their education or training?** 

Specifically, was it:
- **Within the last 20 weeks** (about 5 months ago or less)?
- **More than 20 weeks ago**?

This matters because there's an extension period that may apply if they left education recently.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was more than 20 weeks ago - they left school quite a while back now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

## Why You're Not Eligible

For children aged 16-19 (like Alex at 18), Child Benefit only continues if they are:
- **In approved education or training**, OR
- **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks) and meet certain extension criteria

Since Alex:
- Is not currently in approved education or training, AND
- Left school more than 20 weeks ago

...they don't meet the qualifying conditions for Child Benefit.

## Important Information

**If circumstances change:** If Alex decides to return to approved education or training (such as A-levels, college courses, apprenticeships, or other approved programs), you could become eligible again. You would need to make a new claim at that time.

**What counts as approved education/training:**
- Full-time non-advanced education (A-levels, Scottish Highers, etc.)
- Approved vocational training courses
- The course must be for at least 12 hours per week of supervised study

If you have any questions about this decision or need more information about what might qualify, you can contact the Child Benefit Office or visit GOV.UK for more details.
